questions.stem: Suppose the university newspaper is inviting submissions from the students for its coming edition on the recent development in their hometown.You are now to write an essay for submission. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
Over the past few years, my hometown has undergone remarkable changes. As a student writing for our university newspaper, I would like to share two of them that have impressed me the most: transportation and the environment.

In the past, it used to take us hours of bumpy driving to reach the provincial capital. Now, however, a new high-speed railway gets us there in just two hours, and the widened roads have made daily travel far more convenient. Another change worth mentioning is the environment. The small river that once smelled terrible has been cleaned up, and several green parks have been built along its banks, where families now enjoy walking after dinner.

All these changes have made my hometown a much better place to live in. As someone who grew up there, I feel truly proud, and I firmly believe that it will become even more beautiful and livable in the years to come.

sections.title: Section II Listening Comprehension
sections.note: 听力为历年真题原文，题目与答案为官方标准答案；在线音频由语音合成朗读原文，不是考场录音；换浏览器、换手机都能播。

transcript.text: 1 A police officer in the U.S. stopped a large SUV car that was going very slowly and drifting across lanes on a highway.
He expected to find a driver who was either very drunk or having a medical emergency.
Instead, the officer discovered a five-year-old boy sat on the edge of the driver's seat.
His feet could barely reach the brake, and his head was only just high enough to see out of the windows.
The child had taken the keys to the family car while his teenage sister was napping.
He then drove three kilometers across town before getting on the highway.
The boy later told confused officers that he was planning to travel to California and buy a Lamborghini sports car.
Although he only had three dollars in his wallet, at least he was driving in the right direction.

questions.stem: Why did the police officer stop the SUV car?

options.text: He noticed the driver was too young to drive.
He found there was no one sitting at the wheel.
He thought something must be wrong with the driver.
He saw the driver changing lanes much too frequently.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：A police officer in the U.S. stopped a large SUV car that was going very slowly and drifting across lanes on a highway. He expected to find a driver who was either very drunk or having a medical emergency.信号：开篇即点题、紧跟一句"原以为"的推断 。新闻把核心事件放在第一句：车 going very slowly and drifting across lanes（开得很慢、车道间乱飘）。紧接着 He expected t…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音后面确实揭晓司机是 a five-year-old boy（五岁男孩），A 项 He noticed the driver was too young to drive.（发现司机太小不能开车）就盗用了这个"年龄小"的事实。但那是警察拦车"之后"才发现的真相，并非拦车的原因——拦车时他根本看不清开车的是谁。听到"小孩"就选 A，正中原词陷阱。 借用原文：a five-year-old boy sat on the edge of the driver's seat
optionAnalysis.B: 与原文相反：B 项 He found there was no one sitting at the wheel.（发现没人坐在方向盘后）听起来很像那个离奇画面，但录音说的是男孩 sat on the edge of the driver's seat——其实有人坐在驾驶位，只是个小孩。而且"座位上情况"是拦车后才看清的，拦车当下警察只看到车乱晃。B 既与原文不符、又答非所问。 借用原文：drifting across lanes on a highway
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：D 项 He saw the driver changing lanes much too frequently.（看到司机频繁变道）盗用了原文 drifting across lanes 里的 lanes。但 drifting across lanes 是"车失控地在车道间飘移乱晃"（因为开车的是够不着踏板的小孩），不是司机主动、频繁地变换车道。D 把"失控飘移"偷换成"频繁变道"，看似沾边实则两回事。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a driver who was either very drunk or having a medical emergency ↔ something must be wrong with the driver 具体病况概括成"司机有问题"）

questions.evidenceText: A police officer in the U.S. stopped a large SUV car that was going very slowly and drifting across lanes on a highway. He expected to find a driver who was either very drunk or having a medical emergency.

questions.stem: What did the boy tell the police officers he was planning to do?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：The boy later told confused officers that he was planning to travel to California and buy a Lamborghini sports car.信号：planning to 直接引出打算做的事 。信号词 he was planning to travel to California and buy a Lamborghini sports car 里的 plann…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：B 项 Drive across town.（开车穿过城镇）盗用了原文 drove three kilometers across town 里的 across town。但"开车穿城"是男孩已经做过的事（他已经开了三公里穿过城镇上高速），不是他"打算"做的事。题目问的是 planning to 之后的计划，B 把"已发生"偷换成"打算做"，答非所问。 借用原文：he was planning to travel to California
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：C 项 Leave California.（离开加州）盗用了地名 California，但录音说的是 travel to California（去往加州），方向恰好相反——是去、不是离开。地名一念到极易被耳朵抓住，但方向词（to / leave）被悄悄反转，最易让人误选。 借用原文：while his teenage sister was napping
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：D 项 Visit his sister.（看望他姐姐）盗用了原文出现的 sister。但 sister 在录音里只是"趁姐姐午睡时拿了车钥匙"的背景人物（while his teenage sister was napping），男孩的计划是去加州买跑车，从没说过要去看望姐姐。这是把一个出现过的人名硬塞进"计划"里。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（buy a Lamborghini sports car ↔ Buy a sports car. 去掉品牌名后即同一动作）

questions.evidenceText: The boy later told confused officers that he was planning to travel to California and buy a Lamborghini sports car.

transcript.text: 1 Mobile phones have changed the way we live, how we read, work, communicate, and shop.
But we already know this.

What we have not yet understood is the way the tiny machines in front of us are changing our skeletons, possibly altering not just the way we behave but even the very shape of our bodies. 2 New scientific research at the University of the Sunshine Coast in Queensland, Australia, suggests that young people are developing extra pieces of bone at the backs of their heads.
These pieces of bone are caused by the way people bend their heads when they use the phone.
This shifts weight onto the muscles at the back of the head and causes the bone to grow in a way that is not normal.
This process can be compared to the way the skin hardens in response to constant rubbing or pressure.
The result is a piece of bone like a horn that sticks out from the head by the neck.

questions.stem: What does the report say we have not yet understood about mobile phones?

options.text: How they change the way we shop.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：What we have not yet understood is the way the tiny machines in front of us are changing our skeletons, possibly altering not just the way we behave but even the very shape of our bodies.信号：题干原话 we have not yet understood 直接复现 。录音里 What we have not yet understood is the way the tiny machines in fr…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音开头 how we read, work, communicate, and shop 确实念到 shop 购物，但紧接着说 But we already know this——购物属于 "我们已经知道" 的部分，而题目问的是 "还没理解" 的，正好相反，选它就掉进了原词陷阱。 借用原文：how we read, work, communicate, and shop
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：选项 How they cause increased headaches. 说手机导致头痛增多，但整段录音从未提到 headaches 头痛，是凭 "手机看多了会头疼" 的生活常识硬加的，属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：录音里 how we read, work, communicate, and shop 念到 communicate 沟通，How they affect our communication. 借此设套；但沟通和购物一样属于 But we already know this 已知的部分，不是题问的 "还没理解" 的，故错。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（changing our skeletons ↔ How they alter human skeletons. changing 同义替换为 alter）

questions.evidenceText: What we have not yet understood is the way the tiny machines in front of us are changing our skeletons, possibly altering not just the way we behave but even the very shape of our bodies.

questions.stem: What happens to the skin when rubbed or pressed constantly?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：This process can be compared to the way the skin hardens in response to constant rubbing or pressure.信号：题干关键词 skin、rubbing、pressure 同句聚齐 。录音 the skin hardens in response to constant rubbing or pressure 把题干的 skin、…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：It loosens. 说变松，但录音讲皮肤是 hardens 变硬，没有任何 "变松" 的说法，纯属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：It brightens. 说变亮，录音谈的是皮肤受摩擦后 hardens 变硬的物理硬化，与 "变亮" 毫不相干，录音也未提及。
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：It softens. 变软，恰与录音 the skin hardens 变硬相反。这是预读时就标好的反义诱选——一字方向之差，听不清硬 / 软就会反选。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the skin hardens ↔ It hardens. the skin 由 It 指代、hardens 原词承接）

questions.evidenceText: This process can be compared to the way the skin hardens in response to constant rubbing or pressure.

transcript.text: A village is going to throw a birthday party for an orange cat named Wilbur, who has become famous for making a regular appearance at local shops.
transcript.zh: 一个村庄将为一只名叫Wilbur的橘猫举办生日派对,这只猫因定期光顾当地商店而出名。

transcript.text: Wilbur has his own Internet pages as he approaches his 10th birthday on July 7. Wilbur is both bold and friendly. He spends most of his time in shops and businesses around the village. He'll just take himself into any shop, anywhere. There was one time when the doctor's receptionist came back and he was sitting on her chair. Among his favorite haunts are a local hairdresser, two pubs, and the Nottingham Primary School.
transcript.zh: Wilbur即将在7月7日迎来10岁生日,它有自己的网页。Wilbur既大胆又友好,它大部分时间都在村里的商店和企业中度过。它会自己走进任何商店、任何地方。有一次医生的接待员回来时,发现它正坐在她的椅子上。它最喜欢去的地方包括一家当地理发店、两家酒吧和Nottingham小学。

transcript.text: Lesley Harper, who runs one of the pubs, said the cat has been a big hit with their customers. "He's been a regular visitor for most of this year," she told the Press Association. "He's a very relaxed cat, happy for customers and villagers young and old to come in and say hello." She also said he is a cat of expensive tastes who likes his high priced cat food.
transcript.zh: 经营其中一家酒吧的Lesley Harper说这只猫深受顾客喜爱。她告诉Press Association:"今年大部分时间它都是常客。它是一只非常放松的猫,乐意让顾客和村民不论老少进来打招呼。"她还说它是一只品味昂贵的猫,喜欢吃高价猫粮。

transcript.text: Sarah Godfrey, who is organizing Wilbur's party, told the local newspaper, "Wilbur is part of our lives, as he is for everyone who lives in the village."
transcript.zh: 正在组织Wilbur派对的Sarah Godfrey告诉当地报纸:"Wilbur是我们生活的一部分,对村里每个人来说都是如此。

questions.stem: What does the report say the village is going to do for the cat Wilbur?

options.text: Ask a local pet shop to adopt him.
Name an orange tree after him.
Hold a birthday party for him.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：A village is going to throw a birthday party for an orange cat named Wilbur, who has become famous for making a regular appearance at local shops.信号：开篇 going to 句式即新闻核心事件 。新闻第一句 A village is going to throw a birthday party for an orange cat named Wilbur 用 g…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项 Create Internet pages for him. 借用了第二段 Wilbur has his own Internet pages 这一原词，但原文说的是 Wilbur 已经拥有自己的网页（既成事实），而非村庄「将要为他创建」网页，且这件事不是「村庄为他做的事」，属于答非所问加时态错位的双重陷阱。 借用原文：an orange cat named Wilbur
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：选项 Ask a local pet shop to adopt him. 抓住了录音里反复出现的 local shops 这一概念，但录音从未提及 pet shop 或 adopt——Wilbur 是已经有人照看的明星猫，「让宠物店领养他」是凭借 cat/shops 自行联想的过度推断。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：选项 Name an orange tree after him. 同时盗用了 an orange cat 中的 orange 和 named Wilbur 中的 name，制造「以橘猫之名命名橘树」的错觉，但原文里 orange 修饰的是 cat、name 是给猫命名，与「橘树」毫无关系。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（is going to throw a birthday party ↔ Hold a birthday party for him. throw=hold 的同义词替换）

questions.evidenceText: A village is going to throw a birthday party for an orange cat named Wilbur, who has become famous for making a regular appearance at local shops.

questions.stem: What do we learn from the report about the cat?

options.text: He is a bold and aggressive pet.
He pays regular visits to village shops.
He once bit a doctor's receptionist.
He likes to sit on the hairdresser's chair.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：He spends most of his time in shops and businesses around the village. He'll just take himself into any shop, anywhere.信号：频次副词 most of his time 与范围词 any/anywhere 强调常态 。He spends most of his time in shops and businesses around the …

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：选项 He is a bold and aggressive pet. 盗用了录音里 Wilbur is both bold and friendly 中的 bold，但把后半句的 friendly 偷偷换成了 aggressive。bold 在 friendly 与 aggressive 两种语境下意思走向完全相反，原文明确说他是 bold and friendly（大胆又友好），与 aggressive 截然相反。 借用原文：the doctor's receptionist came back and he was sitting on her chair
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：选项 He once bit a doctor's receptionist. 借用了录音里 the doctor's receptionist came back and he was sitting on her chair 中 receptionist 这一原词，但原文说的是「前台回来时发现他坐在自己椅子上」，根本没有「咬人」这一情节。bite 是凭「猫与人接触」自行加戏的虚构事件。 借用原文：Among his favorite haunts are a local hairdresser
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：选项 He likes to sit on the hairdresser's chair. 把「坐在椅子上」这一情节（原文里发生在 the doctor's receptionist came back and he was sitting on her chair 即医生前台的椅子上）安到了理发店的椅子上。原文只在 Among his favorite haunts are a local hairdresser 里提及理发店是他常去的地方之一，但并未说他喜欢坐理发店椅子。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（spends most of his time in shops and businesses around the village ↔ pays regular visits to village shops. 频次副词 most of his time 与 regular 等值）

questions.evidenceText: He spends most of his time in shops and businesses around the village. He'll just take himself into any shop, anywhere.

questions.stem: What does the pub owner, Lesley Harper, say about the cat?

options.text: He is fond of luxury cat food.
He likes to stay in villagers' houses.
He knows everybody in the village.
He often seeks food around her pub.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：She also said he is a cat of expensive tastes who likes his high priced cat food.信号：She also said 引出直接信息源加 expensive/high priced 同向强化 。She also said he is a cat of expensive tastes who likes h…

optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：选项 He likes to stay in villagers' houses. 借了录音中 happy for customers and villagers young and old to come in and say hello 里的 villagers 一词，但原文说的是「乐于让村民和顾客进店打招呼」——他待的是酒馆，村民是进店打招呼的人，「待在村民家里」这一情节子虚乌有。 借用原文：happy for customers and villagers young and old to come in and say hello
optionAnalysis.C: 过度推断：选项 He knows everybody in the village. 把录音里 happy for customers and villagers young and old to come in and say hello 这种「乐于和顾客与村民打招呼」的描述夸大成「认识村里每个人」。原文从未说他「认识」任何人，更没说 everybody，是典型的范围极大化推断。 借用原文：high priced cat food
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：选项 He often seeks food around her pub. 借了酒馆这一场景设定，但 Lesley Harper 从未说他「在酒馆附近觅食」。原文里关于「食物」的唯一说法是 high priced cat food，重点在「高档」而非「在酒馆附近找」。seeks food around her pub 是把场景与食物两个真实元素硬拼出的虚构动作。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a cat of expensive tastes ↔ He is fond of luxury cat food. expensive tastes 与 fond of luxury 同义概括）

questions.evidenceText: She also said he is a cat of expensive tastes who likes his high priced cat food.

transcript.text: M: So, where do you want to go for lunch?
transcript.zh: M: 那么，你想去哪儿吃午饭？

transcript.text: W: I don't know. Do you have anything in mind?
transcript.zh: W: 我不知道。你有什么想法吗？

transcript.text: M: What about the Sandwich Place on Camden Street?
transcript.zh: M: Camden Street 上的三明治店怎么样？

transcript.text: W: Hmm… No, sorry. I don't feel like sandwiches today. It's a great place, but I think we go there too often.
transcript.zh: W: 嗯……不好意思。我今天不想吃三明治。那地方很不错，但我觉得我们去得太频繁了。

transcript.text: M: That's true. Remember that's where we saw Brigette Clark, the famous movie star.
transcript.zh: M: 确实。还记得我们就是在那儿看到电影明星 Brigette Clark 的。

transcript.text: W: Of course. How could I ever forget? There were crowds of people around her asking for a photo with her.
transcript.zh: W: 当然记得。我怎么可能忘记？当时一群人围着她要跟她合影。

transcript.text: M: What about hamburgers, then? There's that American style diner on the way to the mall.
transcript.zh: M: 那汉堡怎么样？去购物中心路上有家美式餐厅。

transcript.text: W: I like that place. Their chips are great, but their service takes a long time. And I need to get back by 2:30 for a conference call. How about trying something new? We could try Mario's, the new Italian restaurant on the corner. It looks all right. Have you been there?
transcript.zh: W: 我喜欢那家店。他们的薯条很棒，但是上菜要等很久。而且我需要在两点半之前回去开电话会议。要不试试新地方？我们可以去 Mario's，拐角处那家新开的意大利餐厅。看起来不错。你去过吗？

transcript.text: M: No, I haven't, but I've noticed that it has great reviews on the Internet. It's supposed to be one of the best Italians in town. I think Jeremy has been there and said it was amazing. I'm up for that.
transcript.zh: M: 没有，我没去过，但我注意到它在网上评价很好。据说是城里最好的意大利餐厅之一。我想 Jeremy 去过，说那里很棒。我没意见。

transcript.text: W: Cool. Have you asked Jeremy if he would like to come with us?
transcript.zh: W: 好啊。你问过 Jeremy 想不想跟我们一起去吗？

transcript.text: M: I already have. He says he can't. He has brought his own lunch today, so he will stay in. I think his wife made him soup.
transcript.zh: M: 我问过了。他说不行。他今天自己带了午饭，所以要待在办公室。我想是他妻子给他做的汤。

transcript.text: W: Poor Jeremy. His wife is a terrible cook. He should throw that soup in the bin and join us.
transcript.zh: W: 可怜的 Jeremy。他妻子厨艺太差了。他应该把那汤扔进垃圾桶，然后跟我们一起去。

questions.stem: What are the speakers talking about in this conversation?

options.text: When to go for their meal.

questions.analysis: 主旨题。答案句（P1）：M: So, where do you want to go for lunch?信号：开门见山的话题问句 。where do you want to go for lunch? 是对话的第一句，用 So 起头直接抛话题，正是听力主旨题最常用的开头点题信号。后续整段所有讨论（三明治店、汉堡店、意大利餐厅…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：全篇对话围绕选餐厅展开，从头到尾没有任何一句提到由谁来点食物，纯属 Who to order the food. 制造的无中生有。
optionAnalysis.B: 录音里 What about the Sandwich Place on Camden Street? 与 I don't feel like sandwiches today. 确实念到了 sandwiches，Whether to have sandwiches. 就盗用了这个原词，让「听到原词就想选」的考生中招。但实际上三明治只是男方第一个提议的备选之一，被否决后整段对话又讨论了汉堡、意大利餐厅，三明治远不足以代表主旨。 借用原文：I need to get back by 2:30 for a conference call.
optionAnalysis.C: 录音里 I need to get back by 2:30 for a conference call. 出现了具体时间，但那是女方解释自己时间紧、不要选服务慢的店的附带理由，整段对话从未围绕「几点去吃」展开讨论，When to go for their meal. 把次要约束当主线。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（where do you want to go for lunch? ↔ Where to have their lunch. where to go 与 where to have 同义）

questions.evidenceText: M: So, where do you want to go for lunch?

questions.stem: Where did the speakers see Brigette Clark, the famous movie star?

options.text: In the expensive Italian style diner.
At the Sandwich Place on Camden Street.
At the American restaurant they frequent.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P5）：M: That's true. Remember that's where we saw Brigette Clark, the famous movie star.信号：that's where + 回指 。that's where we saw Brigette Clark 用 that's where 把「那个地方」指回上一句男声提到的 the Sandwich Place on…

transcript.text: 1 Artificial intelligence agents play ever more influential roles in our lives.
They do everything from suggesting new friends to recommending purchases.
They're even beginning to drive our cars.
Another role that they are expected to take over is negotiating on our behalf in commercial transactions or legal disputes.
So, it's important to know whether using an artificial intelligence agent might affect how we negotiate.
Research indicates that it does.
In a new study, participants were told to imagine that they were negotiating for something important to them, like a house.
Next they were told either that they would negotiate for themselves, or they would program an artificial intelligence agent to negotiate for them.
Participants then completed a survey indicating how tough, deceptive and pleasant or otherwise they wanted to be, or wanted their agent to be, in the negotiations.
For example, participants could choose to be tough by making an opening demand far greater than what they'd be willing to accept.
They could also choose to express sympathy with their opponent to appear pleasant.

But they could also indicate that they—or their agent—would strategically express anger toward the opponent to gain advantage, or they could opt to convey dissatisfaction with the encounter so that the other party would think they were losing interest.
These are both examples of deceptive strategies.
Participants were more willing to employ deceptive strategies when assigned an agent to negotiate on their behalf.

transcript.text: New research has studied the effects of a seven-week healthy cooking course. Academics measured the program's effect on cooking confidence and self-perceived mental health. Researchers also measured participants' overall satisfaction around cooking and diet-related behaviors.

transcript.text: What were the findings? Course participants saw significant improvements in general health. They also reported improved mental health and subjective vitality immediately after the program. These benefits remained six months after the completion of the course.
transcript.zh: 研究发现了什么?课程参与者的总体健康状况有了显著改善。他们还报告称,在项目结束后心理健康和主观活力立即得到改善。这些益处在课程完成六个月后仍然保持。

transcript.text: What caused these improvements? Researchers have previously found a link between eating more fruits and vegetables, and improved longer term mental health. This would imply that the participants in the current study may have felt better due to improved diet.
transcript.zh: 是什么导致了这些改善?研究人员此前发现,摄入更多水果和蔬菜与长期心理健康改善之间存在联系。这意味着当前研究中的参与者可能因饮食改善而感觉更好。

transcript.text: However, the study showed participants' mental health improved even if their reported diet did not change after completing the program. Also, the mental health benefits were equal among participants who were overweight or obese and those in a healthy weight range. This suggests a link between cooking confidence and satisfaction around cooking, and mental health benefits.
transcript.zh: 然而,研究显示,即使参与者报告的饮食在完成项目后没有改变,他们的心理健康也有所改善。此外,超重或肥胖参与者与体重正常参与者获得的心理健康益处相当。这表明烹饪信心和对烹饪的满意度与心理健康益处之间存在联系。

transcript.text: Who benefits most from learning to cook? Gender plays a part. At the start of the program, 77 per cent of female participants were confident about cooking, but just 23 per cent of males were confident. At the end of the program, cooking confidence and skills were equal across both counterparts. This change in confidence could lead to a gender balance in home cooking. This in turn could reduce consumption of unhealthy, high-calorie processed meals.
transcript.zh: 谁从学习烹饪中受益最多?性别起到一定作用。在项目开始时,77%的女性参与者对烹饪有信心,但只有23%的男性有信心。项目结束时,双方的烹饪信心和技能达到了平衡。这种信心的变化可能导致家庭烹饪中的性别平衡。这反过来又可以减少不健康、高热量加工食品的消费。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the benefits the participants gained from the healthy cooking course?

options.text: They were perceived differently by some academics.
They still existed six months after the course ended.
They varied greatly among the course participants.
They were only measurable within seven weeks.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：These benefits remained six months after the completion of the course.信号：段落收束句 + 时间锚点 six months 。These benefits remained six months after the completion of the course. 是第二段最后一句，承担收…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项里 perceived differently by some academics 听起来像在说“被某些学者看法不一”，它盗用了第一段里 Academics measured the program's effect on cooking confidence and self-perceived mental health. 出现过的 Academics 与 self-perceived，但录音从未说 academics 之间对这些好处有不同看法，是把原文里出现过的词重新拼装成一个新意思。 借用原文：the mental health benefits were equal among participants who were overweight or obese and those in a healthy weight range
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：选项 They varied greatly among the course participants. 说好处在参与者之间差异巨大，但第四段 Also, the mental health benefits were equal among participants who were overweight or obese and those in a healthy weight range. 反而说好处在不同体重人群之间是相等的，方向恰好与本选项相反。 借用原文：a seven-week healthy cooking course
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：选项 They were only measurable within seven weeks. 表面有 seven weeks 这个录音里念到的数字（a seven-week healthy cooking course），听起来像是“原话”。但 seven-week 在录音中只是课程的时长，不是好处的可测时间窗；而且加了 only 限定，与第二段的 six months 直接矛盾。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（These benefits remained six months after the completion of the course. ↔ They still existed six months after the course ended. remained = still existed；completion of the course = course ended）

questions.evidenceText: These benefits remained six months after the completion of the course.

questions.stem: What do the new research findings suggest about mental health benefits?

options.text: They can be easily seen among participants in a healthy weight range.
They should be attributed to participants' change in diet behaviors.
They are linked to cooking confidence and cooking satisfaction.
They actually result from eating more fruits and vegetables.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：This suggests a link between cooking confidence and satisfaction around cooking, and mental health benefits.信号：转折 However 之后的 This suggests 结论句 。第四段首句 However, the study showed participants' mental health improved even …

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项 They can be easily seen among participants in a healthy weight range. 把录音里 the mental health benefits were equal among participants who were overweight or obese and those in a healthy weight range 中的 healthy weight range 摘出来，但录音强调的是“无论超重还是健康体重，效果都相等”——选项却暗示“只在健康体重组里更容易看到”，把“相等”偷换成“在某一组更明显”。 借用原文：participants' mental health improved even if their reported diet did not change after completing the program
optionAnalysis.B: 与原文相反：选项 They should be attributed to participants' change in diet behaviors. 把心理健康益处归给“饮食行为的改变”，但 participants' mental health improved even if their reported diet did not change after completing the program. 直接说“即便饮食没变，心理健康也改善了”——选项与原文方向恰好相反。 借用原文：Researchers have previously found a link between eating more fruits and vegetables, and improved longer term mental health.
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：选项 They actually result from eating more fruits and vegetables. 几乎逐字盗用 Researchers have previously found a link between eating more fruits and vegetables, and improved longer term mental health.，听感非常“对”。但录音明确指出这只是“之前的研究”和“可能的解释”，被第四段 however 推翻；本研究真正的结论是烹饪信心与满足感，而不是多吃果蔬。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（This suggests a link between cooking confidence and satisfaction around cooking, and mental health benefits. ↔ They are linked to cooking confidence and cooking satisfaction. a link between A and B = A are linked to B）

questions.evidenceText: This suggests a link between cooking confidence and satisfaction around cooking, and mental health benefits.

questions.stem: What plays a role in determining who benefits most from learning to cook?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P5）：Who benefits most from learning to cook? Gender plays a part.信号：段首设问 + 直接应答 。Who benefits most from learning to cook? 是段首设问，几乎是把题干 What plays a role in determining who bene…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：选项 Confidence. 与录音 77 per cent of female participants were confident about cooking, but just 23 per cent of males were confident. 中反复出现的 confident/confidence 同根——录音确实在大量谈“信心”，但 confidence 是“差异表现的指标”而非“决定谁受益最多”的那个变量；真正决定的是性别（女生先有信心、男生后追上）。 借用原文：Course participants saw significant improvements in general health.
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：选项 Health. 利用了全文反复出现的 health/mental health/general health 主题词的熟悉感，但录音从未把 health 作为“决定谁受益最多”的变量；恰恰相反，the mental health benefits were equal among participants who were overweight or obese and those in a healthy weight range 还说健康状态不同的人受益是相等的。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：选项 Practice. 的 practice（练习/实践）在录音中没有任何对应：第五段讨论性别差异和家庭烹饪平衡，从未把“练习多少”列为决定受益的变量。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（Gender plays a part. ↔ Gender. 原词直出，无需改写）

questions.evidenceText: Who benefits most from learning to cook? Gender plays a part.

transcript.text: What is personal space? We often think of it as an invisible bubble of space surrounding us that others can't enter, without causing discomfort. Research shows, however, that we actually have bubbles of different sizes. Each of these bubbles applies to a different set of people.
transcript.zh: 什么是个人空间？我们常常认为它是环绕我们周围的一个无形气泡，他人不能进入，否则会引起不适。然而，研究表明，我们实际上拥有不同大小的气泡。这些气泡中的每一个都适用于不同的人群。

transcript.text: The smallest zone, called "intimate space", extends outward from our bodies 18 inches in every direction. Only family, pets and one's closest friends may enter it. A mere acquaintance entering our intimate space makes us uncomfortable. Next is the bubble called "personal space", extending from 1.5 feet to 4 feet away. Friends and acquaintances can comfortably occupy this zone, especially during informal conversations, but strangers are forbidden. Extending from 4 to 12 feet away from us is "social space". Here people feel comfortable conducting routine social interactions with new acquaintances or total strangers.
transcript.zh: 最小的区域称为"亲密空间",从我们身体向外延伸18英寸的各个方向。只有家人、宠物和最亲密的朋友可以进入。仅仅是熟人进入我们的亲密空间就会让我们感到不舒服。接下来是称为"个人空间"的气泡,从1.5英尺延伸到4英尺之外。朋友和熟人可以舒适地占据这个区域,尤其是在非正式交谈期间,但陌生人是被禁止的。从我们4到12英尺之外延伸的是"社交空间"。在这里,人们可以舒适地与新认识的人或完全陌生的人进行日常社交互动。

transcript.text: Those are the average sizes of American's personal bubbles, anyway. It is important to keep in mind that personal space varies depending on culture and context. Furthermore, there are significant individual differences. As we all know, cultural or individual differences in personal bubble diameters are all too often the cause of discomfort. How did these personal bubbles arise? According to research, we begin to develop our individual sense of personal space around age 3 or 4. The sizes of our bubbles are fixed by our teens. These bubbles are constructed and monitored by the brain region involved in fear.
transcript.zh: 无论如何,这些是美国人个人气泡的平均大小。重要的是要记住,个人空间因文化和环境而异。此外,还存在显著的个体差异。众所周知,个人气泡直径的文化或个体差异往往是造成不适的原因。这些个人气泡是如何产生的？根据研究,我们在3岁或4岁左右开始发展我们个人的个人空间意识。我们气泡的大小在青少年时期就固定下来了。这些气泡是由与恐惧有关的大脑区域构建和监控的。

questions.stem: What does research show about our personal space?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Research shows, however, that we actually have bubbles of different sizes.信号：Research shows + however 转折 。答案句一头连了两个强信号：Research shows 是题干 What does research show 的原句对应，however 是转折信号，转折之…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项 It keeps others away. 借用了原文 others can't enter 里的 others 来制造『听到 others 就想选』的诱惑；但原文说的是『别人进不来（指气泡的功能描述）』，并不是『研究发现』那条结论。研究发现的真意在转折 however 之后，不在转折之前。 借用原文：without causing discomfort
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：选项 It causes discomfort. 抓住了原文 without causing discomfort 里的 discomfort 来制造原词陷阱；但原文是说『别人进入气泡会带来不适』，描述的是『进入气泡的后果』，不是研究本身的结论。这条信息在 23 题才用得上，放到 22 题就是张冠李戴。 借用原文：an invisible bubble of space
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：选项 It remains visible. 说气泡『一直可见』，而原文 an invisible bubble of space 明确说 invisible（看不见）。选项盗用了气泡这个话题，却把极性反过来了，是典型的极性反转陷阱。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（bubbles of different sizes ↔ It varies in size. bubbles of different sizes = varies in size）

questions.evidenceText: Research shows, however, that we actually have bubbles of different sizes.

questions.stem: What happens if a mere acquaintance enters our intimate space?

options.text: It renders the acquaintance a stranger.
It brings the acquaintance closer to us.
It causes the bubble around us to vanish.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：A mere acquaintance entering our intimate space makes us uncomfortable.信号：题干定位词原句重现 。录音里 A mere acquaintance entering our intimate space 几乎是题干 a mere acquaintance enters our intimate…

optionAnalysis.B: 过度推断：选项 It renders the acquaintance a stranger. 借用录音里反复出现的 acquaintance 和 strangers 来制造『听到原词就选』的诱惑；但原文从未说『熟人会变成陌生人』，只是分别为不同人群分配了不同空间。从『让人不适』推到『熟人变陌生人』属于过度推断。 借用原文：makes us uncomfortable
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：选项 It brings the acquaintance closer to us. 说『把熟人拉近』，但原文 makes us uncomfortable 明确说会让我们不适，属于结果方向反了。同时它盗用了 acquaintance 这个原词来骗你选。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：选项 It causes the bubble around us to vanish. 借用整组核心词 bubble 来吸引点击，但录音从未说过『熟人进入亲密空间会让气泡消失』，只是说会让我们不舒服。bubble vanish 这一结果属于原文未提及。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（makes us uncomfortable ↔ It makes us feel uncomfortable. 几乎逐词对应）

questions.evidenceText: A mere acquaintance entering our intimate space makes us uncomfortable.

questions.stem: Where do people feel comfortable interacting with new acquaintances or strangers?

options.text: Over 2 feet away from one another.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：Extending from 4 to 12 feet away from us is "social space". Here people feel comfortable conducting routine social interactions with new acquaintances or total strangers.信号：题干关键词原句重现 + 空间命名句 。录音里 new acquaintances or total strangers 几乎与题干 new acquaintances or strangers 一字不差对应；这句又紧…

optionAnalysis.A: 张冠李戴：选项 In personal space. 借用了原文中的 personal space 这个原词，但录音里 personal space 是给『朋友和熟人』用的（friends and acquaintances 在『informal conversations』里使用），并不是给陌生人用的。配的人群对不上。 借用原文：18 inches in every direction
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：选项 Within a distance of 18 inches. 盗用了录音 18 inches 这个原词数字，但原文里 18 inches 是给 intimate space 的尺寸（只允许家人、宠物和最亲密的朋友进入），与题干问的『陌生人交往的距离』完全不是一回事。 借用原文：Extending from 4 to 12 feet away from us is "social space"
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：选项 Over 2 feet away from one another. 里的 2 feet 看起来很像录音里反复出现的几个距离数字，但录音里给陌生人/新熟人互动的距离是 4 to 12 feet，不是 2 feet。选项偷偷把数字换小了，是典型的数字偷换。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（"social space" ↔ In social space. 专有概念名直接对应）

questions.evidenceText: Extending from 4 to 12 feet away from us is "social space". Here people feel comfortable conducting routine social interactions with new acquaintances or total strangers.

questions.stem: When are the sizes of our bubbles fixed?

options.text: When we begin to feel fear.
When we develop a sense of space.
When we are 3 or 4 years old.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：The sizes of our bubbles are fixed by our teens.信号：题干原句重现 + 关键介词 by 。录音 The sizes of our bubbles are fixed by our teens 几乎逐词复述题干 the sizes of our bubbles fixed…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项 When we begin to feel fear. 盗用了录音 the brain region involved in fear 里的 fear 来吸引点击，但原文从未把 fear 当作一个时间节点，只是顺带提到大脑里负责恐惧的区域参与构建气泡。这是把『脑区话题』偷换成『时间节点』。 借用原文：we begin to develop our individual sense of personal space around age 3 or 4
optionAnalysis.B: 答非所问：选项 When we develop a sense of space. 盗用了录音 we begin to develop our individual sense of personal space 里的 develop 和 sense of space，但这一句对应的动作是 develop（开始发展），不是题干问的 fixed（被定型）。同一段里两个动作各配一个时间，选项把动作和时间故意错配。 借用原文：around age 3 or 4
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：选项 When we are 3 or 4 years old. 直接盗用了录音里的数字 around age 3 or 4，但这个年龄绑的是『开始发展空间感』(develop)，不是『定型』(fixed)。题干问的是 fixed 的时间，故 3 or 4 岁是错配。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（by our teens ↔ When we enter our teens. 介词短语 ↔ 时间状语从句）

paragraphs.text:
A number of studies have looked at how family life can affect productivity and satisfaction in the workplace. However, there has been 26______ little research on the influence of leisure activities. So Ciara Kelly and colleagues recruited 129 hobbyists to look at how the time spent on their hobbies 27______ their work life.

The researchers found that when participants spent longer than 28______ on their leisure activity, their belief in their ability to perform their job was strengthened. But this was only the 29______ when they had a serious hobby that was dissimilar to their job, or when their hobby was similar to their work but they only did it 30______ . When their hobby was both serious and similar to their job, then spending more time on it actually decreased their work 31______ .

Why might that be? To maintain a serious hobby, people need to invest significant psychological resources, say the authors—so if the activity has the same kinds of demands as their work, they may be left 32______ and unable to perform well at their job. But if their hobby is quite different from their career, it may not 33______ in the same way but instead help them develop other knowledge and skills that can 34______ their confidence at work. "Consider a scientist who is a keen rock climber," says Kelly. "Since climbing is so far 35______ from their day-to-day work activities, they can still recover from the demands of their job with plenty of resources."

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 26.
questions.analysis:
【答案】O（官方答案）
应填 O) surprisingly
【原文】However, there has been __(26)__ little research on the influence of leisure activities：However 表明"家庭对工作影响研究很多，却出人意料地少有关于休闲的研究"——surprisingly（令人惊讶地）正强调这种"本该有却很少"的反差。
C) casually 语义不搭（随意地）：casually"随意地"修饰人做事的方式，casually little research 讲不通——研究数量"少"与"随意"无关，逻辑不成立。

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 27.
questions.analysis:
【答案】N（官方答案）
应填 N) shaped
【原文】to look at how the time spent on their hobbies __(27)__ their work life呼应开篇 how family life can affect productivity——研究的正是爱好时间如何"影响、塑造"工作生活。shape（塑造、影响）与 affect 同义，是本句最贴的谓语动词。
M) scratch 词义不搭：scratch"抓挠"，scratch their work life 语义荒谬，与"研究爱好如何影响工作"无关，纯靠词性蒙的人最易在此掉坑。

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 28.
questions.analysis:
【答案】I（官方答案）
应填 I) normal
【原文】participants spent longer than __(28)__：longer than normal 是地道说法，意为"花的时间比平常（正常水平）更长"，normal 正好充当"平常"这个比较基准，与下文"花更久会增强工作信心"衔接。
K) relative 被 longer 诱导但不成基准：relative"相对的/亲戚"，句中有比较级 longer 易让人误以为"相对"很搭，但 longer than relative 既不表常态也不成搭配，无法作"比平常更久"的基
J) prevalent 义为"普遍的"，不搭：prevalent"普遍流行的"，longer than prevalent 讲不通，与时间长短的比较基准无关。
L) removed 义为"远离的"，留给 35 空：removed"远离的"用于 far removed from，longer than removed 不通；它是第 35 空的答案。

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 29.
questions.analysis:
【答案】B（官方答案）
应填 B) case
【原文】But this was only the __(29)__ when…：this was only the case when… 意为"只有在…时才是这种情况"，the case 是地道固定搭配，承接上句"花更久会增强信心"并加上限定条件。
E) estate 词义离题：estate"房地产"，the estate 与本句"这只在…时成立"的逻辑毫无关系。
G) faculty 义偏不搭：faculty"教员/才能"，this was the faculty 不成话，无法表"情况如此"。

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 30.
questions.analysis:
【答案】C（官方答案）
应填 C) casually
【原文】hobby was similar to their work but they only did it __(30)__与前半句 a serious hobby（认真的爱好）对照：but they only（只是）暗示这里是"不认真、随便玩玩"，casually（随意地）正好。
hobby was similar to their work but they only did it __(30)__与前半句 a serious hobby（认真的爱好）对照：but they only（只是）暗示这里是"不认真、随便玩玩"，casually（随意地）正好。

questions.stem: Choose the word for blank 31.
questions.analysis:
【答案】D（官方答案）
应填 D) efficiency
【原文】与 work 搭配且贴合"损耗工作表现"主线
B) case 搭配与逻辑都不合：case"情况"，decreased their work case 不成搭配，"减少工作情况"逻辑讲不通；case 该留给 the case 那种框架（第 29 空）。
E) estate 词义离题（房地产）：estate意为房地产、庄园，work estate 不成搭配，更与全文"爱好—工作信心"主题毫无关系，纯属凑数干扰。
G) faculty 义偏且不搭：faculty常指大学教员或人的官能/才能，work faculty 不是地道说法，也无法承接"多花时间在爱好上反而减少了什么"的语境，逻辑接不上。

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Attitudes towards paternity leave(陪产假) have drastically changed in America in the last five years as more fathers feel comfortable taking extended time off, but gender bias persists when it comes to career prospects and the home, according to a new study of working parents.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Research by the Boston College Center for Work & Family, which surveyed new parents at four large US companies who were qualified for taking at least six weeks paid parental leave, found that 81% of the 1,240 employees surveyed said the notion of fathers taking leave has become more acceptable.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Of those surveyed, 62% of fathers took the maximum amount of time off compared to 93% of mothers, and around three-quarters of workers said their employer was equally supportive of mothers and fathers taking parental leave and over half said leave policies had made workplace culture better.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The US is one of only three countries in the world not to offer statutory(法定的) paid leave, but increasingly states and companies are starting to take up the issue. So far, eight states and the District of Columbia have their own paid family leave laws.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Brad Harrington, executive director of the center and lead author of the study, estimates only 20% to 30% of companies in the US offer paid parental leave. He feels the research findings reflect an obvious change in corporate attitudes to new fathers taking time off.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: "We did a study on paternity leave five years ago. Compared with those findings, these numbers were shocking to me. I did not expect 80% of people to say the organisation finds dads taking this leave acceptable and three-quarters to say it's equally supportive of women and men taking leave," Harrington said.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The previous study found that nearly three-quarters of fathers saw two to four weeks as an appropriate duration for paternity leave and 76% said they would prefer not to take all their time off at once.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Since then, there have been a number of legal cases against companies involving paternity leave—including cases against JPMorgan Chase and Estee Lauder—which have helped put pressure on companies to make their parental leave policies gender neutral.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: However, the study also shows how traditional gender roles endure both at work, where more women than men reported changes in their perceived career potential, and at home—even among workers who claim to have a strong desire for equality.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: The vast majority of men, 97%, said one of the top reasons to take leave was to share caregiving with their partner. But when they were asked about how caregiving and household tasks were divided, their answers painted a different picture. While about 75% of employees said both genders should give the same amount of care, the majority of men and nearly half of women admitted that in reality the female actually did most of it. A tiny fraction, 2%, of men said they did more of the childcare.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Men and women's experiences of the return to work following parental leave were also considerably different. Of the women surveyed, 32% reported a downturn in their job satisfaction, while 14% said it increased. In comparison, 17% of men said their job satisfaction went down and 20% said it went up. Meanwhile, more women reported an increase in their responsibilities and manager expectations after childbirth. Half of the women said they used flexible work arrangements after becoming a parent, while just 27% of men did. Similar percentages of men and women said they enjoyed their careers and that it gave them a sense of achievement, while around half of women and 44% of men said it was a key part of their identity.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: On the subject of career advancement, 59% of women and 49% of men said leave could be limiting and both genders said they feared it would have an impact on their progress long-term. But on opportunity for promotion, more than double the number of women, 30% compared with 15% of men, believed their chances to be lower after becoming a parent. Despite progress, the struggle for women to reach the highest positions of power is demonstrated in this year's Fortune 500 list, which featured a record 33 female CEOs, but this still represents a tiny fraction of the total.

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: Harrington said culture change depends on companies putting more focus on men and their responsibilities. "By that I mean companies need to give men paternity leave and encourage men to take time off to be with their kids early on in the kids' life. They also need to recognise that men have to make significant adjustments when they become parents. Companies cannot do all these things to enhance women's advancement and then turn around and say, 'Oh, but we don't expect the men to take over for the women at home.'"

paragraphs.label: N
paragraphs.text: In May, the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) and Outten & Golden LLP announced a historic class-action $5m settlement with JPMorgan Chase on behalf of male employees who claim they were illegally denied access to paid parental leave. Derek Rotondo, 35, filed the discrimination charge against his company after he was allegedly told by his HR department that mothers were considered primary caregivers. Thus, they were allowed to take 16 weeks of paid parental leave. Fathers, however, could take just two weeks.

paragraphs.label: O
paragraphs.text: The father of two from Columbus, Ohio, who still works at the company as an associate and investigator, said he has witnessed a "domino effect(多米诺效应)" across companies since the settlement, but that there is still substantial progress to be made towards changing attitudes towards paternity leave.

paragraphs.label: P
paragraphs.text: "I do think there's still some way to go…there's still going to be sort of the unstated expectation for new dads to essentially come right back to work, but I think the research is showing that's starting to change." He said equal parental leave is an essential component to creating gender equality in the workplace. "The old standard of women staying home, having babies and cooking doesn't apply and hasn't applied for a long time."

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Having a rival can keep you committed to achieving your goals and enhance your overall performance. But before you go out and find an entrepreneur to outcompete, it's important to understand and avoid the traps that often come with rivalry. After all, competitive rivalry can also hinder effective decision-making and increase your willingness to take risks, behaviors that can ultimately hurt your venture's success.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Finding someone you're committed to outcompeting can be a great way to stay focused on your goals and push your venture to the next level. But when you're intently focused on outperforming your rivals, you may begin to develop a "win-at-all-costs" mentality that causes you to ignore how you achieve success. One group of researchers, for example, examined the link between rivalry and unethical behavior. They found that when people compete against their rivals, they are more willing to behave unethically to win. But such behavior may stain your reputation and strain relationships important to your success. One way to avoid this trap is to stop and reflect on what's important. While outperforming your rivals may provide short-term benefits, the loss of your integrity will have long-term consequences.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: One reason having a rival can enhance your venture's performance is that it creates a level of excitement that drives you to work harder. But this eagerness to win may also hurt your venture's success, particularly when it causes you to make impulsive, insensible decisions. But it's possible to avoid such costly mistakes by making a habit of engaging in critical thinking, such as considering opposing viewpoints and conducting cost-benefit analyses, especially for those decisions that are complex and can determine the future of your venture.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The sense of eagerness that comes with having a rival can not only cause you to make poorer decisions, but it can also lead you to take greater risks that put your venture in peril. One way you can overcome the risk-inducing effects of rivalry that stand to endanger your venture's success is to remain attentive to your emotional state and actively monitor how such feelings are affecting your decision-making.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: A multitasker is one who can perform two or more tasks effectively at the same time, which—apart from the obvious differences—is similar to what a computer does. The concept does indeed come from the realms of technology, where it is used to refer to an operating system that can execute multiple tasks at the same time. However, the question is: can a person really be a multitasker?

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: For most scientists, the answer is no. So much so that, according to experts in neuroscience(神经系统科学), our brains do not handle multitasking situations well. As soon as two tasks require our attention, productivity suffers. What we call multitasking, therefore, is in reality the ability to move more or less quickly from one task to another. This requires two essential conditions: that one of the tasks needs to be automatic, like walking or eating, and that they both need different mental processes. Answering the phone and writing at the same time, for example.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: However, on the other side of the coin there are people who maintain that it is possible to be, or at least seem to be, multitasking. A recent study concluded that regardless of whether people are actually handling several tasks or not, the mere fact that they perceive this activity as multitasking has a positive effect on their performance.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The business perspective offers a different view: multitasking is understood as the ability to adapt to all types of environment within a company and effectively undertake different activities within a set time frame. Indeed, many companies look for people who are skilled in multitasking to improve their productivity. From this different perspective, you can not only be multitasking but this ability can also be taught: something that is easier in fluid organisations, which favour flexibility in their working practices.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The benefits of multitasking are clear. Being quicker and more efficient increases our performance and the number of tasks completed. But having to pay attention to several things at once means that the powers of concentration are reduced and that can lead to more mistakes.

改革开放以来，中国人的饮食(diet)发生了显著变化。过去由于经济落后，食品种类有限、数量不足 ，人们仅仅满足于吃得饱。如今中国经济快速发展，食品不仅更加丰富多样，质量也大幅提高。随着生活水平不断提升，人们对饮食的要求越来越高，更加注重吃得营养健康。因此，目前市场上推出的低脂、低糖、有机食品受到人们的普遍欢迎。
questions.analysis:
【参考译文】
Since the reform and opening-up, the diet of Chinese people has undergone significant changes. In the past, due to the backward economy, food was limited in variety and insufficient in quantity, so people were content with merely having enough to eat. Today, with China's economy developing rapidly, food is not only more abundant and diverse but also greatly improved in quality. As living standards keep rising, people have increasingly higher demands for their diet and pay more attention to eating in a nutritious and healthy way. Therefore, the low-fat, low-sugar and organic food launched on the market today is widely welcomed by people.
